overview: This table holds the health, guard, down-gauge, and timing settings used for fighters in battle.
description: Core per-character/per-mission combat parameters: a single 122-row FName-keyed table supplying health, guard durability, down-gauge values and several timing constants to character setup and status controllers. Three fields have no traced native consumer in the reconstructed source.

Id.simple: The name that picks which fighter or mission uses these combat values. Missions can choose a different name to use another set.
Id.technical: FName at row offset 0x8, declared UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadWrite, EditAnywhere) and named by ImportKeyField=Id; the export writes the key as ID and all 122 rows have row name == ID. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows searches the ordered CharacterBaseParameterDataTables array using GameCharacter_Override(Overrides.BaseParameterIdOverride, CharacterRow->Id_CharacterBaseParameter): NAME_None means use the default, and a miss returns false from ResolveDataRows and then ApplyCharacterSetup (no assertion in the reconstruction). Mission overrides reach BaseParameterIdOverride through GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideIds(MissionCharacter.Id_CharacterBaseParameter); PvE and UI paths separately look up the same row from Character.Id_CharacterBaseParameter. Lookup stops at the first matching table; no duplicate-key handling is present.

HitPoint.simple: The fighter's normal maximum health. A larger number means more health, and solo or mission settings can change the final total.
HitPoint.technical: float at row offset 0x10 (constructor default 0). ApplyHitPointParameters first uses Setup.HitPointOverride when > 0; otherwise it uses HitPoint_Solo when Setup.SoloSide == 1 and HitPoint in all other cases, assigning both HitPointMax and current HitPoint. GamePvE_CalcMissionCharacterHitPoint uses HitPoint_Solo/HitPoint only when MissionCharacter.HitPoint <= 0 (not only when the side is non-solo), while PvE ally/Tag setup passes GamePvE_CalcHitPoint(Base->HitPoint, ...) as a positive override that supersedes the solo selection. Command-list and versus-enemy UI also read this raw column as a gauge base. Export values span 150-2000 across 36 distinct positive values.

HitPoint_Solo.simple: Maximum health when the fighter has no teammate. A larger value means more health in that situation.
HitPoint_Solo.technical: float at row offset 0x14 (constructor default 0). It is selected by the same ApplyHitPointParameters branch as HitPoint when Setup.SoloSide == 1, and by GamePvE_CalcMissionCharacterHitPoint's fallback for mission characters; a positive Setup.HitPointOverride wins in both paths. In the export it equals HitPoint in all 122 rows (CP_010: 440), and PvE ally/Tag setups compute their override from Base->HitPoint, so the exported Solo column is not independently exercised there. BattleFree's SoloSide table marks exactly the one-member sides with true.

AttackRange.simple: A stored attack reach value for each fighter. What distance it affects in play is unclear.
AttackRange.technical: float at row offset 0x18 (constructor default 0); exported values are 1000.0 (67 rows), 1250.0 (51), 1050.0 (3) and 2000.0 (1), with CP_010 = 1250.0. No named read of FGameDataTableRow_CharacterBaseParameter::AttackRange was found in reconstructed Source/Plugins. Nearby distance logic instead uses Character.AutoAttackDash_Distance, AttackSet.AttackRangeType plus the action controller's bInEnemyAttackRange/bInAllyAttackRange flags, and per-AI hard-coded CloseAttackRange values; none reads this row. The unit and gameplay purpose are therefore not asserted, and retail Blueprint/engine-side references were not inspected.

Guard_Minimum_Time.simple: The shortest time a ground or aerial guard must be held before release can finish. A larger value slows the release.
Guard_Minimum_Time.technical: float seconds at row offset 0x1C (constructor default 0); all 122 exported rows use 0.2. FGameCharacterAction_Guard::Tick and FGameCharacterAction_GuardAir::Tick enter the release branch only when Elapsed > this value and GuardRigidityTime <= 0.0f; if the Guard key is no longer held they play the guard-end animation and signal GAISlot186(9,3,false,false) (GuardAir also sets its finished flag). CP_180's GuardAir override repeats the same predicate with its own animations. The comparison is strict, so a value exactly equal to the threshold does not yet qualify.

GuardDurability.simple: The guard gauge's starting strength. A larger value lets the fighter block more before the guard breaks.
GuardDurability.technical: float at row offset 0x20 (constructor default 0). UpdateGuardDurability caches it as GuardDurabilityBase and sets CurrentGuardDurability = GetGuardDurabilityMaxRate() * GuardDurability; SetGuardDurability and the regen tick clamp to the same rate-scaled maximum. AI value conditions 23 and 31 divide self/target CurrentGuardDurability by this unscaled row value. Guard-hit FX use NewHitPoint / GuardDurability with FX_CP_000_03111 for >= 0.6, FX_CP_000_03121 for >= 0.3 and FX_CP_000_03131 below that. Blocked-hit damage is subtracted from the current gauge in GameBattleDamage. Export values are 150.0 in 119 rows and 160.0 in 3; no exported row is zero, although the CDO default would be a zero denominator for the AI divisions.

GuardDurability_Solo.simple: A separate guard value is stored for fighters fighting alone. It matches the normal guard value, and its effect is unclear.
GuardDurability_Solo.technical: float at row offset 0x24 (constructor default 0), exported 150.0 in 119 rows and 160.0 in the same 3 rows as GuardDurability; it always equals GuardDurability in this export (CP_010: 150.0). Every named native row read found uses GuardDurability for the status cache, AI denominators and guard-hit FX; no Source/Plugins read of GuardDurability_Solo or solo-side substitution for durability was found. Its native purpose is therefore unresolved rather than proven unused, and retail Blueprint/engine-side references were not inspected.

GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime.simple: A saved guard recovery timing value for every fighter. What it changes in play is unclear.
GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime.technical: float at row offset 0x28 (constructor default 0), exported 3.0 in all 122 rows including CP_010. The name suggests seconds, but no C++ condition, timer or delay consumes it: the Tick checks only bGuardDurabilityRegenEnabled == 1 and bGuardDurabilityRegenBlocked == 0, then reads GuardDurability_Recover. No named Source/Plugins read of this field was found and the reconstructed Tick has no hidden wait timer; retail Blueprint/engine references were not inspected. The serialized value is retained, but its native purpose is unresolved.

GuardDurability_Recover.simple: How quickly the guard gauge refills when the fighter recovers. A larger number makes it refill more slowly.
GuardDurability_Recover.technical: float at row offset 0x2C (constructor default 0), exported 15.0 in all 122 rows. When regen is enabled and not blocked, CurrentGuardDurability is below the rate-scaled maximum, and Recover > 0, Tick adds (100.0 / Recover) * DeltaTime (about 6.67 durability units per second for 15.0) and clamps to [0, GetGuardDurabilityMaxRate() * GuardDurability]. A zero CDO would skip the division and disable this path; no exported row is zero.

DownValue.simple: The stamina-like gauge that wears down before a fighter is knocked down. A larger value lets them take more hits.
DownValue.technical: float at row offset 0x30 (constructor default 0). ApplyDownValueParameters copies it to DownValueMax and SetDownValue (current gauge); InitializeStatus and ResetDownValue also copy it to AdaptDownValue/AdaptDownValueMax and set AdaptHitPoint = max(HitPoint - DownValue, 0). Armor/blocked-hit processing subtracts attackerScale * DamageRow.Down_Damage * receiver GetDownDamageRate from the current gauge; the shikigami damage path subtracts DamageRow.Down_Damage directly. Zero triggers down handling and RestartDownValueRecover, and AI checks current DownValue against DownValueMax. Export values span 180.0-2000.0, with 1000.0 in 112 rows; later DownValue reads on the status controller are cached state, not row reads.

LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime.simple: For large fighters, this sets the wait before the down gauge refills, and zero gives no timed refill. One fighter uses this for adaptation.
LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime.technical: float seconds at row offset 0x34 (constructor default 0). RestartDownValueRecover, when DownValueMax > DownValue and bRefill == false, sets DownRecoverTime from this column if Owner.Get()->GetActionSlot146() is nonzero, otherwise from Global.DownValue_Recover_Time. Tick counts that timer down by DeltaTime * DownRecoverRate and calls ApplyDownValueParameters only after it crosses from positive to <= 0; therefore CP_010's exported 0.0 does not mean an immediate refill in this reconstruction - with the large-character flag set and bRefill false it leaves the timer at zero and no timed refill is started. bRefill true still refills immediately and returns. CN_240's ATTACKK_1 also passes this row value to BeginAdaptation as AdaptDelayTime. Export: 0.0 in 111 rows, 5.0/7.0/10.0/15.0 in the remaining 11.

notes: AttackRange, GuardDurability_Solo and GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime have verified retail offsets and serialized values, but no named native consumer was found in reconstructed Source/Plugins; their gameplay meaning is not asserted, and retail Blueprint/engine-side references were not inspected.

The solo flag is FGameCharacterStatusSetup.SoloSide == 1; BattleFree/PvE setup maps one-member sides to true. For health, a positive Setup.HitPointOverride wins first, PvE ally/Tag setup supplies one computed from HitPoint, and mission fallback or no-override setups can use HitPoint_Solo. No solo substitution exists for guard durability in the reconstruction.

The export is one CharacterBaseParameterDataTable with 122 rows; every row name equals its ID, ImportKeyField is Id, and the 46 by-character shard copies reproduce subsets with identical values. 119 exported rows are referenced by CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterBaseParameter or MissionCharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterBaseParameter; three are not.

All consumer descriptions come from reconstructed C++ (AGENTS.md states Blueprints contain no logic); layout-check references prove field name/offset only, not byte-match or behavior. No retail Blueprint graphs or uncooked asset internals were inspected directly.
Constructor defaults are 0.0 for all ten numeric fields; those are CDO values, not the exported row values.

usages.detail: Resolves the CharacterBaseParameterDataTable primary asset and adds it to the ordered CharacterBaseParameterDataTables array (+0x3F0).
ResolveDataRows finds the row by override-first ID and caches the pointer in AGameCharacter::BaseParameterRow (+0x3A8); a miss makes character setup fail.
Copies MissionCharacter.Id_CharacterBaseParameter into FStudioBattleCharacterOverrides.BaseParameterIdOverride, so mission rows can replace the character's default parameter row.
ApplyHitPointParameters gives a positive Setup.HitPointOverride priority, then chooses HitPoint_Solo or HitPoint by SoloSide.
ApplyDownValueParameters initializes DownValueMax and current DownValue from the row.
UpdateGuardDurability caches GuardDurability as GuardDurabilityBase and initializes the current gauge through the rate multiplier.
Selects a guard-hit effect from NewHitPoint / row GuardDurability thresholds 0.6 and 0.3.
Blocks the ground guard-end transition until Elapsed > Guard_Minimum_Time and rigidity has ended.
CP_180's GuardAir override applies the same minimum-time and rigidity predicate with character-specific animation names.
Regenerates guard durability using (100 / GuardDurability_Recover) * DeltaTime when enabled, unblocked and below the scaled maximum.
Applies armor/down damage to the current down gauge using attacker scale, DamageRow.Down_Damage and the receiver's down-damage rate.
Selects LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime for large-character down recovery instead of the Global row's time, with a zero value leaving no timed refill.
Counts DownRecoverTime down by DeltaTime * DownRecoverRate and refills the down gauge only when the positive timer expires.
Passes LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime into CN_240 BeginAdaptation as AdaptDelayTime for ATTACKK_1.
Mission-character HP fallback reads HitPoint_Solo or HitPoint only when MissionCharacter.HitPoint <= 0.
PvE solo allies use raw Base->HitPoint as the seed for a positive HitPointOverride after growth/equipment/vow calculations.
PvE Tag allies use the same Base->HitPoint-derived override path.
Interval PvE reads Base->HitPoint to recalculate current and maximum HP between stages.
Command-list UI resolves the row directly from Character.Id_CharacterBaseParameter and uses HitPoint as the raw gauge width.
Versus-enemy settings UI resolves the row and feeds HitPoint into its PvE gauge preview.
AI value conditions 23 and 31 normalize current guard durability by this row's unscaled GuardDurability.
AI down-gauge decisions compare status DownValue with the DownValueMax seeded from this row.
